General Motors is rolling out a CarPlay compromise on two truck models, appearing to gradually walk back its earlier decision to drop support for the feature.

New reports indicate the automaker is developing a dedicated interface for its trucks that will include CarPlay……

GM was the first to announce back in 2023 that all its future EVs would abandon CarPlay, and it subsequently trotted out a string of frankly absurd explanations and justifications. Many consumers were unhappy, and a significant number said they would not buy another GM vehicle until the policy was reversed.

We previously saw the first crack in the company's CarPlay ban involving one of its most expensive luxury EVs, though the company offered no explanation for that exception.

TNW now reports that the company is developing a new in-vehicle infotainment interface for its trucks that will support both CarPlay and Android Auto. The compromise is that neither system will be able to occupy the entire screen.

The company likewise offered no explanation for this apparent exception, saying only that it wanted to spare customers too many steps.

The report also notes growing government concern over reliance on touch screens for critical vehicle functions such as horns, turn signals and hazard lights. Both the EU and China now require physical buttons for some controls, in order to reduce the time drivers spend looking away from the road and into the cabin.
